headline: US Crude Inventories Fall by 5.27 Million Barrels
summary: American Petroleum Institute data shows United States crude oil inventories decreased by 5.267 million barrels in the week ending October 30, following a prior decline of 2.031 million barrels.
why: Crude oil inventory data is a key indicator of supply and demand dynamics in the global energy market, frequently influencing oil price volatility for professional energy traders.

impacts.name: WTI Crude
impacts.why: A larger-than-expected decline in crude oil inventories signals robust demand or lower supply, which typically supports upward price pressure on crude oil futures.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: A significant drop in commercial crude inventories points to tightening near-term supplies, which structurally supports commodity prices.
